text:
Thomas Harley is back to logging the minutes of a No. 1 defenseman in Dallas: 25:27 a night on the season, 26:29 over the last ten, with a 30:55 night against Florida on November 15. His best moment came in Vegas on November 19, a late equalizer from distance that pushed the game to overtime before Tyler Seguin won it in the shootout.

The numbers are solid without being loud. He has 15 points in 25 games, a pace above last season's 36 in 70, and the Stars take 52.7% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him at five on five, 4.7 points better than without him. His shooting is right at league average for defensemen, so there's no bubble in the line.

The question is defense. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more with him on the ice last season, bottom 10% among defensemen, in a year he was around replacement level overall. This season's on-ice share says that's improved. Friday's loss in St. Louis was his third straight game without a point, but our range for his season sits at 40 to 60 points.
